title: Community Suggestions and Tags
summary: How to write useful TheySix suggestions and what the suggestion status tags mean.

body.text: Suggestions should be respectful, specific, and easy to evaluate. Posts that violate the community guidelines may be locked or removed, and duplicate suggestions make it harder to track useful ideas.

items: Explain the idea clearly enough that someone else can picture the result.
Search for existing suggestions before posting a duplicate.
Do not bump a suggestion unless you are adding useful information.
Keep replies relevant to the suggestion rather than starting an unrelated discussion.
Implemented: the feature has been added.
Accepted: TheySix intends to implement it if practical; timing is not guaranteed.
Undetermined: the idea looks promising but still needs review for feasibility or balance.
Denied: the idea is not planned because it is unsuitable, impossible, or too difficult.
Duplicate: the suggestion already exists and the thread may be locked.
Unmarked: the suggestion has not been reviewed yet or does not fit another status.

body.text: Many suggestions may be read without receiving a status tag. Tags are used as a planning aid, not as a promise that every accepted idea will ship immediately.
